ComplexHeatmap Heatmap Layer Processor

Source: R/complexheatmap_heatmap_layer_processor.R
ComplexHeatmapLayerProcessor.Rd

Reads the heat layer of one ComplexHeatmap heat map from the HeatmapList its drawing returned (complexheatmap_capture()): the one heat map of a chart, or one of a list's.

Order. The rows and columns are read in the order drawn, the heat map's own row and column order in the drawn list: by the dendrograms when clustered, by row_order/column_order when given, and in a list by the order the list shares – the main heat map's rows in a horizontal list, its columns in a vertical one. Rows are top first, as maidr.js reads data.points.

Splits. A heat map split into slices (row_split, row_km, column_split, column_km) is read as one grid, its slices put side by side in the order drawn, top to bottom and left to right. The gaps between slices are not cells, and are not read: moving past the last row of one slice reaches the first row of the next.

Values. Each cell is the value of the heat map's own matrix (the matrix slot), exactly; a missing or infinite value is a hole (null). A value the colour mapping clips is still its own value, not the end of the scale.

Labels. The row and column labels drawn (row_labels, column_labels, which default to the matrix's dimnames); when the names are not shown (show_row_names = FALSE), the matrix's dimnames; and for an unnamed matrix, each row's or column's number in the matrix.

Selectors. Each cell is selected by its own id, in a grid whose rows run bottom first, as maidr.js's heat grid does. When the body was drawn as a raster image there are no cells to select, and the layer is read without highlighting; a message (class maidr_complexheatmap_raster) says so.
